Definition: a idol; also, a pain or wound
BiblicalUsage: This word holds two meanings that meet in the heart: an idol and a sorrow. The psalm says the sorrows of those who hasten after another god will be multiplied, the same psalm says God heals the broken in heart and binds up their wounds, the proverb says he that winks with the eye causes sorrow, and Job says he is afraid of all his sorrows.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the two meanings are one warning, because the idol that promises comfort only multiplies sorrow, and the God who was forsaken for it is the only One who binds the wound. The sorrows of the idolater and the wounds of the broken are both healed in the same place, and I hold that He is near to both.
